name: Tuvia Flees the House in the Rain
description: Tuvia runs away from the house as rain pours heavily. Water streams down the roof and splashes against the ground, soaking the path ahead. Tuvia moves quickly, disappearing into the downpour.
related_events: Tuvia runs away from the house during heavy rain

name: Tuvia Hears Talk of His Parents' Death
description: Tuvia stands nearby as people talk casually about the death of his parents. The conversation continues without noticing his presence, and he remains silent, listening.
related_events: Tuvia hears casual discussion about his parents' death

name: Climbs ladder and finds hidden people
description: He climbs a ladder and is startled to find five more men and women in hiding. They stare in mute terror.
related_events: Character climbs ladder and discovers hidden individuals

name: Tuvia Anchors the Wire
description: Tuvia and Asael lie on one side of the road. Tuvia takes one end of a wire and loops it around a post, securing it firmly in place.
related_events: Tuvia secures wire around post

name: Zus, Peretz, and Jacov Secure the Wire to the Tree
description: Zus, Peretz, and Jacov worked together to wrap a wire around the trunk of a tree, looping it tightly and securing it in place. They adjusted their positions to ensure the wire held firm, pulling it taut and fastening it to the branches above.
related_events: Zus, Peretz, and Jacov attach wire to a tree

name: Tuvia Sets a Wire Trap for the Approaching Bike
description: Tuvia waits until the bike is nearly upon them. Then, he tightens a wire, stretching it invisibly across the road.
related_events: Tuvia stretches wire across the road to intercept approaching bike

name: Tuvia Bielski Hides from Patrol in Doorway
description: Tuvia Bielski, wearing the torn remains of his uniform, moves quickly and quietly along a cobble-stoned street. He presses himself into a doorway as a patrol approaches and passes by, remaining still until the danger has moved on.
related_events: Tuvia Bielski evades patrol by hiding in doorway

name: Tuvia Stands in the Rain Before the Lit Windows
description: Tuvia stands in the driving rain, his body shaking. He stares at the lit windows, rain falling heavily around him.
related_events: Tuvia stands in the driving rain while shaking
Tuvia stares at the lit windows

name: Driver Stops for Downed Motorcycle
description: The vehicle approaches on the dark road, headlights sweeping forward. As the light falls on a motorcycle lying on the pavement, the driver slows, steers toward the shoulder, and brings the vehicle to a stop at the side of the road.
related_events: Vehicle approaches and detects downed motorcycle
Driver slows and pulls vehicle to the side of the road

name: Koscik and Tuvia Argue as Refugees Watch
description: Koscik and Tuvia stand close, speaking in harsh whispers. Koscik warns that if the laborers find the hidden people tomorrow, he will be denounced. Tuvia resists, asking how he is supposed to feed them, saying he can't even care for his own family. Behind them, several refugees step out from their hiding place. They remain silent, their eyes fixed on Tuvia with a bitter, resentful gaze.
related_events: Koscik and Tuvia argue about hiding refugees
Refugees emerge from hiding and observe Tuvia

name: Zus and Asael Find the Massacre Site
description: Zus and Asael stand frozen before a trough, their eyes fixed on a pair of motionless legs. Beyond, the torso of a man lies in the dirt. Dead livestock sprawl across the ground, swarmed by buzzing flies. A woman's body rests nearby. The air hums with insects, thick with the stillness of death.
related_events: Zus and Asael discover dead bodies among livestock
Flies swarm around dead livestock and human remains

name: Run Through the Bombs
description: Bombs explode all around as he runs past dead bodies and burnt-out vehicles. He throws off a World War II-era Red Army helmet, shrugs out of a field jacket, and drops a heavy pack—anything that slows him down. Without breaking stride, he glances over his shoulder. The sky above is filled with bombers. He keeps running.
related_events: Character runs through war-torn area amid ongoing bombings
Character discards military equipment to aid escape
Character looks back at approaching bombers

name: Zus and Asael's First Attempt to Get Food
description: Zus and Asael arrive at a building to find food. Zus enters the structure while Asael stays outside, standing watch. Asael scans the surroundings, alert and tense, as Zus searches inside.
related_events: Zus and Asael attempt to obtain food at a location
Asael stands guard outside while waiting

name: Captain Reveals Missed Targets After Ditch Capture
description: The police captain and Kosciuk sit together, drinking vodka. The captain recounts how he caught five people hiding in a ditch, the stench so strong he worried the Germans wouldn't take them. Kosciuk jokes they might accept them at a reduced price, and both laugh. The captain then asks if Kosciuk knows the Bielskis. When Kosciuk says he does, the captain reveals they missed two of them during the raid on the parents' home. The two continue drinking, the mood unchanged, laughter mixing with the clink of glasses.
related_events: Police captain captures five people hiding in a ditch
Police captain mentions missing two individuals during raid on parents' home
Group reacts with laughter and drinks more vodka after grim remark

name: Man Coughs and Shrugs, Tuvia Glances in Disapproval
description: A man coughs, then shrugs as if to apologize. Tuvia looks at him and glares.
related_events: Man coughs and apologizes with a shrug
Tuvia glares at the man

name: Asael and Zus Flee with Belongings and Mezuzah
description: Asael, loaded with possessions, hurries toward the woods. Zus stops briefly at the door, pries the mezuzah from the frame, and then follows.
related_events: Asael hurries back to the woods carrying possessions
Zus removes the mezuzah from the door

name: Zus Restrains Asael During Breakdown
description: Aron sits motionless, staring straight ahead. Asael trembles violently, tears streaming down his face as he gasps and sobs. Zus, unable to reach him with words, steps forward and grabs him, pulling him into a tight hold that hovers between restraint and comfort. Asael continues to rock, half-resisting, half-collapsing into the embrace.
related_events: Zus attempts to calm Asael
Asael breaks down in grief and panic
Zus restrains Asael in a conflicted embrace

name: The Captain's Wife Pleads for Death
description: The police captain's wife kneels beside the bodies of her dead family, wailing in Russian. Tears stream down her face as she cries out, 'Kill me, too!' Tuvia stands over her, silent and unmoving. He leans in and demands, 'Tell them who did this.'
related_events: Police captain's wife keens over dead family
Wife begs Tuvia to kill her
Tuvia demands identification of perpetrator

name: Roundup in the Shtetl
description: Local police moved through the shtetl alongside German soldiers, pulling Jewish residents from their homes and forcing them into lines in the square. Peasants stood on the edges, striking the captives with sticks as they passed. One man broke away, running toward an alley, but was chased down and beaten until he fell. The others were pushed onto trucks idling nearby, their doors slamming shut as the engines started.
related_events: Local police assist Einsatzgruppen in rounding up Jews
Peasants attack Jews with sticks during roundup
Jewish man attempts to escape and is beaten
Jews are loaded onto waiting trucks

name: Tuvia Seeks Rest and Forgiveness in the Forest
description: Tuvia pushes through a dense forest, branches scraping against his face as he moves. He reaches a tree and leans against it, catching his breath. Closing his eyes, he whispers, 'Riboynoy shel oylam, riboynoy shel oylam... Lord of the universe, forgive me, I have murdered — but they were monsters and did not deserve to live.'
related_events: Tuvia pushes through dense forest while being scratched by branches
Tuvia leans against a tree to rest
Tuvia prays to God for forgiveness

name: Zus Hears a Noise and Finds Aron in the Root Cellar
description: A noise comes from the cupboard. Zus grabs a hatchet and moves toward the sound. From the root cellar, a young boy, Aron, emerges. His face is dirty, streaked with tears. The family steps forward to embrace him, but Aron flinches away. He does not speak. He looks around, disoriented, as the candles flicker on the dinner table.
related_events: Zus grabs hatchet in response to noise from cupboard
Young boy emerges from root cellar in disoriented state
Aron recoils from attempted embrace by family

name: Zus Raises Rifle After Confrontation With Anti-Semite
description: After a tense encounter, Zus raises his rifle in triumph. He threatens to crush a man's head, muttering curses against Poles, his voice filled with anger. Tuvia objects, questioning whether the plan is to terrorize every anti-Semite in Belorussia. Zus responds without hesitation: some will be killed.
related_events: Zus threatens to crush man's head and expresses hatred toward Poles
Zus raises rifle in triumph after confrontation
Tuvia challenges Zus's strategy of terrorizing anti-Semites
Zus declares intention to kill some anti-Semites

name: Tuvia and Companions Confront and Kill the Truck Owner
description: A man runs out of a tavern shouting about his truck. Tuvia, Zus, and the others emerge from the shadows. The man freezes when he sees their weapons and asks who they are, then says they forced him to give up his truck. Zus fires his gun. Jacov and Peretz shoot as well. The man falls dead. They lift his body and throw it onto the burning truck.
related_events: Man runs out of tavern shouting about his truck
Tuvia and companions reveal themselves from the shadows
Man expresses fear and claims coercion
Zus, Jacov, and Peretz shoot the man
Man's body is placed on burning truck

name: Tuvia Learns the Truth About His Parents' Killers
description: Tuvia asks Koscik if certain men were the ones who killed his parents. Koscik hesitates, then nods in confirmation. The two men embrace silently. Tuvia then leads the group forward toward the woods.
related_events: Koscik confirms that certain men killed Tuvia's parents
Tuvia and Koscik share a moment of emotional solidarity

name: Tuvia Leads the Group into the Woods
description: After speaking with Koscik, Tuvia turns and walks toward the woods, and the group follows. Pinchas Zucker is there, leading a tethered goat. Another man carries a violin case. Koscik hands Tuvia another bottle of vodka before they part. Tuvia moves ahead, guiding the group beneath the tree line and into the forest.
related_events: Tuvia leads his group toward the woods

name: Zus and Peretz Retreat Shooting, Announce Bielski Otriad
description: Zus and Peretz back out of an open doorway, firing into the building behind them as screams echo from inside. Nearby, faces appear at the windows of surrounding houses, watching cautiously. Zus turns toward the neighborhood, shouting that they are the Bielski Otriad, that they are Jews, and that if the people want to kill Jews, here they are. Tuvia looks around, his expression wary, as the tension in the air thickens.
related_events: Zus and Peretz retreat while firing into a building
Residents cautiously observe the confrontation from nearby windows
Zus declares Bielski Otriad's presence to the neighborhood
Tuvia expresses concern over escalating situation

name: Tuvia Dresses and Departs as Rifka Stays Behind
description: Tuvia puts on his clothes while Rifka stands by the window, smoking a cigarette. They talk about the danger of being sent to the ghetto and the possibility of using false papers to pass as gentiles. Tuvia shakes his head when Rifka suggests it for him. Once dressed, he tells her he needs to go see to his family and asks if she will come with him to the countryside. Rifka declines. She remains by the window as he leaves.
related_events: Tuvia prepares to leave while discussing danger with his wife Rifka
Rifka offers to stay with Tuvia for the night
Tuvia decides to prioritize his family over staying with his wife
Rifka refuses to accompany Tuvia to the countryside

name: Tuvia Returns to His Brothers
description: The sound of a footstep breaks the silence. Asael and Aron sit up in fear. Tuvia steps forward, saying, 'If I was a German, you are dead.' Asael leaps to his feet and throws his arms around Tuvia, crying, 'Papa and Mama. They killed them.' He clings to Tuvia as if he were salvation. Aron, too, allows himself to be held. Tuvia embraces them both without speaking. Then Zus appears, holding a hatchet. 'Big brother returns,' he says. He looks at Tuvia warily. 'You saw them?' Tuvia nods. 'Yes. I saw them.' Zus reaches into his pocket, pulls out a mezuzah, and tosses it to Tuvia. 'Welcome home,' he says.
related_events: Asael reacts to Tuvia's return with emotional embrace
Tuvia silently comforts his brothers
Zus confronts Tuvia upon his return
Zus returns the mezuzah to Tuvia

name: Zus and Asael Confront Farmer Walencki at the Barnyard
description: Zus and Asael move cautiously through a barnyard. A tethered dog barks furiously as they approach. Farmer Walencki steps forward, brandishing a pitchfork, and demands in Russian to know what they want. Asael replies in Russian, asking for food. Walencki warns them that people are searching for them and tells them to leave. Zus takes a threatening step toward the farmer, but his younger brother, Asael, holds him back. As they retreat toward the woods, Zus calls out, 'We'll be back.'
related_events: Tethered dog barks at approaching brothers
Farmer Walencki confronts Zus and Asael with a pitchfork
Asael requests food from the farmer
Zus threatens the farmer before being restrained by Asael
Zus warns the farmer they will return

name: Ambush and Kill the Courier
description: The courier's bike crashes as he hits the wire. The Bielski fighters rush forward, swarming him. One fires the last bullet from the Mahkarov rifle, killing him. ZUS searches the saddlebags of the fallen bike and pulls out a knife, holding it up. Peretz points toward the road—more headlights are approaching fast. Tuvia shouts, 'Hide! Everyone!' They scramble back into the ditch, dragging the dead courier with them.
related_events: Bielski fighters ambush and kill the courier

name: Zus Searches the Saddlebags and Finds a Knife
description: After the courier falls, his bike sliding away, Zus rummages through the saddlebags. He pulls out a beautiful knife and lifts it up. Headlights approach in the distance. Tuvia calls for everyone to hide. They scramble into the ditch, dragging the dead courier with them.
related_events: Zus searches the courier's saddlebags

name: Hide from Approaching Headlights
description: Peretz spots more headlights rapidly approaching. Tuvia shouts for everyone to hide. The group scrambles back into the ditch, dragging the dead courier with them.
related_events: Peretz spots approaching headlights
Tuvia orders the group to hide
Group retreats into the ditch with the dead courier

name: Koscik Greets the Police Captain and His Sons
description: Koscik stands near a car as a Belarusian police captain and his sons step out. They exchange greetings in Russian. Koscik notes they are working late. The police captain replies that they have been hunting Jews, adding that their new bosses are very organized. Koscik offers a bottle, saying the hunt must have made them thirsty. The captain says they killed fifteen Jews in one day and that the council is offering a year of free taxes for each Jew turned in. Koscik asks if a Jew is worth that much and jokes whether they pay more for a fat one. The men laugh.
related_events: Koscik greets Belarusian police captain and his sons
Police captain reveals hunting Jews for rewards
Koscik makes sarcastic remark about value of Jews

name: Koscik Offers a Bottle After the Hunt
description: Koscik greets a Belarusian police captain and his sons as they step out of a car. Speaking in Russian, Koscik remarks that they are working late. The police captain responds that they have been hunting Jews, adding that their new bosses are very organized. Koscik holds out a bottle, offering it to them. He says hunting can work up a thirst. The police captain mentions they caught fifteen Jews in one day and that the council is offering a year's free tax for each Jew turned in. Koscik asks if a Jew is worth that much and jokes whether they pay more for a fat one. The men laugh.
related_events: Koscik offers bottle to police captain and sons

name: Aron plays with a stick and follows a mysterious figure
description: Aron stands alone in the woods, holding a stick he pretends is a gun. He moves from tree to tree, making shooting sounds. He stops suddenly, seeing a dark blur shift among the trees. He crouches low, watching. The shape moves away. Aron begins to follow it, stepping carefully through the undergrowth.
related_events: Aron mimics shooting a stick like a gun while creeping through trees
Aron spots a moving dark blur in the trees and begins to follow it

name: Aron Waves to the Small Girl Who Runs Away
description: Aron tracks a dark shape through the trees and sees it is a small girl about his age. He waves to her. She stands still, staring at him without speaking, then turns and runs into the woods. Aron immediately follows, moving quickly after her.
related_events: Aron encounters a small girl in the woods and waves to her
The small girl stares at Aron and runs away

name: Aron discovers a mass grave in the woods
description: Aron chases the small girl into a secluded wooded grove and suddenly stops, frozen by the sight of a trench overflowing with naked corpses. The small girl runs to a middle-aged man wearing a tattered coat with a crude Star-of-David sewn onto it. He holds an older girl in his arms. Around them, several other emaciated figures emerge from hiding, their bodies gaunt, their clothes in rags, moving slowly among the dead.
related_events: Aron chases the small girl into a wooded grove and discovers a pile of corpses
The small girl reunites with a middle-aged man wearing a Star-of-David
Starved survivors emerge from hiding near a mass grave

name: Taxi Ride to the Doctor
description: A taxi pulls up to the curb in the rain, where an elderly man and his middle-aged son are waiting. They get into the back seat, and the son tells the driver, '23rd and Lex.' He turns to his father and asks, 'How ya doin', Papa, you doin' alright?' The old man replies, 'Fine, fine.' The son says it's just a check-up, that Doctor Katz says he'll outlive them all. He looks out the window and comments that the traffic isn't bad, they should be back in time to watch the Mets.
related_events: Taxi arrives at curb to pick up elderly man and his son
Middle-aged son gives destination to cab driver
Middle-aged son checks on his father's well-being
Middle-aged son mentions doctor's appointment and baseball game

name: Elderly Man Recognizes Cab Driver's Name
description: The elderly man sits in the back of the taxi, his eyes fixed on the cab driver's hack license. Rain taps against the windows as the car moves through the city. He leans forward slightly, squinting at the name—'Bielski.' His breath catches. The middle-aged son, noticing his father's stillness, turns to him. 'Papa? What is it?' The old man doesn't look away from the mirror. 'You. Can it be?' The cab driver's eyes meet his in the rearview, then flick away, then return. 'Bielski. Can it possibly be?'
related_events: Elderly man stares intently at cab driver's hack license
Middle-aged son asks his father what is wrong

name: Recognition in the Rearview Mirror
description: The elderly man stares at the cabby's hack license, then looks up to meet his eyes in the rearview mirror. 'You. Can it be?' he says, his voice trembling. 'Bielski. Can it possibly be?' The cab driver looks away, then slowly turns his gaze back toward the old man. A desperate, rasping pant echoes as the camera closes in on the driver's eyes.
related_events: Elderly man recognizes cab driver as Bielski
Cab driver avoids and then returns eye contact with elderly man
Desperate panting sound is heard during mirror close-up

name: Zus and Tuviya Argue Over Vengeance
description: Zus loads Wilencki's gun, working to open the breach. Tuviya tells him they must get what they need without killing, reminding him that nothing will bring their family back—Mama, Papa, none of them. Zus responds that it's blood for blood, and that Tuviya already had his revenge. Tuviya says he still sees their faces. Zus asks who said 'Vengeance is mine,' and when Tuviya questions if Zus believes he is doing God's work, Zus replies that only Tuviya plays God—saving some, taking others. Tuviya warns they cannot become like their enemies. Zus says if only that were possible, then looks at Tuviya and asks if he is coming with them. He names Peretz, Jacov, and Asael. Tuviya turns to Asael, who looks away, then asks Zus if he is making the decisions now. They stand in silence, locked in a tense exchange. Tuviya finally says they will wait for dark.
related_events: Zus loads Wilencki's gun while Tuviya argues against killing
Tuviya questions the morality of vengeance
Zus invokes divine vengeance in justification of his actions
Zus accuses Tuviya of playing God through selective life and death decisions

name: Zus Challenges Tuviya's Authority
description: Zus loads Wilencki's gun and focuses on opening the breach. Tuviya urges the group to take what they need without killing, warning that violence won't bring back their family. Zus responds with 'Blood for blood,' saying Tuviya already had his revenge. Tuviya replies that he still sees their parents' faces. Zus asks who said 'Vengeance is mine,' then states that only Tuviya plays God, saving some and taking others. Tuviya insists they must not become like their enemies. Zus replies, 'If only,' and gives a hard look before asking if Tuviya is coming with them. He names Peretz, Jacov, and Asael as part of the group. Tuviya glances at Asael, who looks away, then turns back to Zus and asks, 'You are making the decisions now?' The two men lock eyes in silence, neither yielding. Finally, Tuviya says, 'We wait for dark.'
related_events: Zus challenges Tuviya's leadership and asserts decision-making authority
Tuviya resists Zus's assertion of authority and questions command structure
Tension escalates between Zus and Tuviya over group leadership

name: Tuviya Delays the Group's Movement Until Nightfall
description: Despite the tension between them, Tuviya tells the group they will wait for dark before taking any action. He turns away, signaling the decision is final.
related_events: Tuviya decides to delay the group's movement until nightfall

name: The Naming of the Bielski Otriad
description: Jacov and Peretz eat, taking ravenous bites. Jacov asks what the name of their otriad is. Asael interrupts, asking what an 'otriad' is. Tuvia replies that it is an armed brigade. Jacov mentions hearing that the Russians are beginning to organize, both here and in the Lipicanska. Asael then declares, 'Then we are the Bielski Otriad,' and asks if they want to join.
related_events: Asael asks for definition of 'otriad'
Tuvia defines otriad as armed brigade
Jacov inquires about the name of the otriad
Asael declares group identity as Bielski Otriad

name: Jacov and Peretz Seek Partisans
description: Jacov and Peretz sit together, eating between bites. Peretz says they are looking for partisans. Jacov asks Tuvia the name of his otriad. Asael asks what an otriad is, and Tuvia replies that it is an armed brigade. Jacov says they heard the Russians are beginning to organize here and in the Lipicanska. Tuvia looks surprised, asking if this is true. Asael then declares, "Then we are the Bielski Otriad." He turns to Jacov and Peretz and asks if they want to join. Peretz glances around and says the Russians are fighters, but adds that you need a gun to join them—without a gun, you are nothing. He notes that the Russians sabotage railroads and kill Germans. Just then, Zus speaks from above, his voice firm, saying they will kill all the Germans the others can handle, starting that night. They look up at him, seeing his face covered in blood and filth. Zus adds that it’s doable, if they’re not afraid to use a rifle.
related_events: Peretz declares search for partisans
Jacov reports Russian partisan organization

name: Zus Challenges the Group to Take Up Arms
description: Zus appears above the group, his face covered in blood and dirt. From off-screen, he announces that he and his men will kill all the Germans the others can handle, starting that night. He looks down at them and issues a challenge: if they are not afraid to use a rifle, they can join the fight.
related_events: Zus declares readiness to kill Germans starting that night
Zus challenges group to use rifle without fear

name: Koscik Gives Tuvia Bullets
description: Koscik, a rotund, florid-faced Pole, hands four bullets to Tuvia, saying he has only these. Tuvia takes them and thanks him deeply. They sit in Koscik's warmly-lit kitchen, where Koscik's wife stands by the stove, silent and glaring at Tuvia. Koscik remembers Tuvia's father as a good man, and Tuvia says his father spoke the same of Koscik. Koscik pulls out a bottle of vodka, tells Tuvia to ignore his wife, and raises the bottle in a toast to the dead. He offers vodka to his wife, but she only glares.
related_events: Koscik hands bullets to Tuvia
Tuvia expresses gratitude to Koscik

name: Koscik and Tuvia Remember the Dead
description: Koscik hands Tuvia a small bundle of bullets and looks at him with solemn recognition. They sit together in the warm light of the kitchen, the air thick with unspoken history. Koscik speaks first, saying Tuvia's father was a good man. Tuvia replies that his father had said the same about Koscik. A bottle of vodka appears on the table. Koscik raises it in a toast, saying, 'To the dead. God rest their souls,' and offers a drink. Outside, headlights sweep across the window as a car approaches quickly. Koscik's expression changes. He tells Tuvia to hide, pointing toward the barn.
related_events: Koscik recalls Tuvia's father

name: Tuvia and Koscik in a Tense Kitchen
description: Koscik hands Tuvia four bullets. They sit in the warmly-lit kitchen, where Koscik's wife stands by the stove, silently glaring at Tuvia. Koscik recalls Tuvia's father as a good man, and Tuvia returns the sentiment. Koscik produces a bottle of vodka, calls his wife a bitch, and tells Tuvia to ignore her. He raises the bottle in a toast to the dead, speaking in Russian, and offers Tuvia vodka. His wife continues to glare. Headlights sweep across the window as a car approaches quickly. Koscik tells Tuvia to hide in the barn.
related_events: Koscik's wife glares at Tuvia and remains silent

name: Koscik Shares Vodka with Tuvia
description: Koscik takes out a bottle of vodka and raises it in a toast to the dead. He offers a drink to Tuvia, calling his wife a bitch and telling Tuvia to ignore her. His wife stands by the stove, silent and glaring. Headlights suddenly sweep across the window as a car approaches quickly. Koscik tells Tuvia to hide in the barn.
related_events: Koscik offers vodka to Tuvia

name: Koscik Sends Tuvia to Hide
description: Headlights sweep across the window as a car speeds toward the house. Koscik's expression tightens. He turns to Tuvia and says sharply, 'Hide yourself. ...The barn.'
related_events: Headlights sweep over the window as a car approaches quickly
Koscik tells Tuvia to hide in the barn

name: Tuvia's Return and the Brothers' Questions
description: Asael asks Tuvia if he is going back to the army, and Tuvia replies that there is no army anymore. Asael, looking up to his older brother, asks what it was like to be in a war. Tuvia says it wasn’t war—it was something else. Zus watches him closely. Tuvia asks where Sonia and the baby are, and Zus tells him they are hiding in a cellar in Horodysze, and that he will bring them when it is safe. Tuvia asks about Rifka. Zus replies that she is in Novgrudok and refused to leave. Tuvia says she is still his wife. Zus adds that she is still his rich wife, chewing with open mouth as he speaks. He then asks Tuvia why he has come back. Tuvia does not answer, only looks at him. Zus asks if he has a plan. Tuvia says no, and asks if Zus does.
related_events: Asael and Tuvia discuss the nature of war

name: Tuvia Asks About Sonia and the Baby
description: Tuvia asks where Sonia and the baby are. Zus tells him they are hiding in a cellar in Horodysze and says he will bring them when it is safe.
related_events: Tuvia inquires about Sonia and the baby
Zus reveals Sonia and the baby are hiding in Horodysze

name: Zus Questions Tuvia's Return
description: Zus asks Tuvia why he has come back, chewing with an open mouth as he studies him. He presses Tuvia on whether he has a plan, but Tuvia answers no. Tuvia looks at his younger brothers, silent. The question hangs in the air, unanswered, as the moment settles between them.
related_events: Zus questions Tuvia about his return and intentions

name: Tuvia Reveals Rifka's Whereabouts and Their Separated Status
description: Tuvia tells Zus that Rifka is still in Novgrudok and that they remain separated, though she is still his wife. Zus chews his food with an open mouth and calls her Tuvia's 'rich wife,' his tone laced with sarcasm.
related_events: Tuvia reports Rifka is in Novgrudok and remains separated from him

name: Tuvia Asks About Food, Finds Sausage Gone and Worms in Potatoes
description: Shivering and cold, the group tries to start a fire, but Asael's matches are wet. Tuvia asks if there is anything left to eat. Asael checks his bag and finds only a few potatoes, writhing with worms. He says Zus finished the last of the sausage. Tuvia turns to Zus and glares at him. Zus glares back.
related_events: Tuvia asks if there is any food left
Asael reveals Zus ate the last of the sausage
Worms are discovered in the remaining potatoes
Tuvia and Zus exchange hostile glares

name: Zus Proposes Raiding Wilencki's Farm
description: Shivering and hungry, the group searches for food. Asael finds only a few potatoes, crawling with worms. Tuvia asks if there is anything left to eat. Zus says he finished the last of the sausage. Asael’s matches are wet and useless. Zus suggests Stankowicz’s farm, but Asael warns there are dogs. Zus dismisses the danger and shifts the plan to Wilencki’s farm. Tuvia questions how they will get food from Wilencki, asking if he will just give it to them. Zus says they will take it. Tuvia worries Wilencki will call the police. Zus replies that he has spent his life running from the police and sees no reason to stop now. Asael adds that they know the woods and can hide. Tuvia looks at his brothers, silent. The decision is made.
related_events: Zus suggests raiding Stankowicz' farm

name: Tuvia Confronts the Police Captain and Kills Him and His Sons
description: Tuvia stands at the doorway of the Police Captain's home, drenched from the rain, a pistol at his side. The Captain, his wife, and their two sons look up from dinner. Tuvia asks if the Captain knows who he is. The Captain says nothing. His wife grows frightened. One of the sons starts to rise, but Tuvia turns the gun on him and orders him to sit. The Captain continues to chew his food. Tuvia demands to know if the Captain remembers why he is there. The Captain claims he was only doing his job. Tuvia accuses him of hunting Jews. The Captain says he would have lost his job otherwise and insists he was always fair to Tuvia’s family, letting things pass, and tells Tuvia to ask his father. Tuvia snaps, placing the pistol against the Captain’s forehead and shouting for him to get on his knees. The Captain begins to weep. Tuvia declares the names of his parents, David and Beila Bielski, and his brothers. The Captain pleads for his life. One of the sons moves toward Tuvia. Tuvia shoots him in the chest. The mother screams. The Captain starts to stand. Tuvia steps back and shoots him, then shoots the second son. The gunfire stops. The family lies dead.

Tuvia begins stuffing provisions into a sack. Zus turns to the farmer and asks where his gun is. The farmer says he has none. Zus grabs a dinner plate and smashes it into the farmer's face, demanding again to know where the gun is. The farmer, holding his bloody face, pleads with them. Zus kicks him. Tuvia calls out to Zus. Zus kicks the farmer again. The farmer weeps and says the gun is above the stove. Zus kicks him aside, climbs up, and takes an old rifle from above the stove. He points it at the farmer and says they were never there.

Zus kicks him, demanding the weapon again. The farmer pleads, begging for mercy. Zus kicks him once more. The farmer begins to weep. Zus dumps the remains of the farmer's meal over him. Zus threatens to hit him again, warning of worse consequences. The farmer, trembling, points to a rifle above the stove. Zus kicks him aside, climbs up, and takes the rifle. Tuvia sits by the fire. Without a word, Zus reaches for the pistol in Tuvia's belt, pulls it free, and opens the cylinder. He sees there is only one bullet inside.

Zus takes the pistol from Tuvia's belt and checks the cylinder. 'Only one bullet left,' he says. Tuvia replies, 'His sons.' Zus nods. 'How was it?' he asks. 'To kill them. It was good, no?' description: Zus looks around at the sleeping group and asks what they will do with the others. He points out that the women and the old teacher will slow them down. Tuvia responds with sarcasm, mocking Zus’s concern about the teacher. They both agree they need to keep moving quickly. Tuvia suggests sleeping farther up the trail, leaving the others behind where they are. If anyone comes, the gunshots from an attack on the others will give them time to escape. Zus agrees, saying no more will be done after this. Tuvia says, 'No more.'

description: Tuvia stumbles into camp carrying a heavy sack of provisions, followed by a group of new arrivals. He greets those present and begins introducing the newcomers. He points to Tamara, a pleasant-looking woman with a quiet demeanor, and says she is his cousin. He then gestures to Lazar, calling him Isabel's youngest, and directs them both to sit by the fire. Next, he introduces Isaac Malbin from Minsk, a man with a sweet face and round glasses. As the group settles, Tuvia calls out for Asael, instructing him to find food for the newcomers. While the introductions unfold, Zus exchanges a look with Tuvia and pulls him aside for a quiet word. Nearby, a dark-haired woman passes by, drawing Zus's attention. Around the fire, the others begin asking the newcomers questions about their hometowns and whether certain people have survived.

Tuvia interrupts, 'They are family.' Zus presses, 'And how will we feed this family?' Tuvia replies, 'We'll water the soup.' Nearby, a dark-haired beauty passes by, drawing their attention. name: Tuvia and Shimon Reunite in the Forest
description: Tuvia leads his group through the forest. An old man, Shimon H'aretz, stares at him and speaks, recalling that Tuvia used to sit in the back of the classroom. Tuvia looks at him without responding at first. Shimon says he thought Tuvia was dead. Tuvia replies that he thought the same about Shimon. Shimon says he is at least half-dead, then mentions he heard about Tuvia’s parents and offers his sorrow. Tuvia shakes his head. Shimon asks about Tuvia’s brothers, remembering one as the wild one. Tuvia tells him Zus is with the other two. Shimon asks if they are hiding in the forest. Tuvia nods. Shimon asks if they’ve had trouble with the police. Tuvia does not answer. Shimon says going to the forest is a wise choice. Tuvia replies that Shimon, once a teacher, now calls him wise despite once thinking Tuvia a dumb schoolboy. Shimon says he spent his life teaching others the right way to live, certain of what was God’s way, but recent events have shaken that certainty. Tuvia says it’s just like school—he doesn’t know what Shimon is talking about. He touches Shimon’s arm and tells him to come, gesturing to the others to follow.

He tries to return a bottle to Koscik, who tells him to keep it. The Captain jokes about being bribed and suggests there might be more black market vodka hidden in the barn. Koscik challenges him to take a look, adding that he should clean out the cow manure while he’s back there. The officer laughs, climbs into his car, and asks Koscik to stay alert. Koscik responds, 'Good hunting.'

Asael then says he can’t believe their father is gone, and the mood shifts as the reality of their loss returns.

Zus, standing nearby, mocks them, calling them little shits and challenging whether they have the nerve to shoot him. In response, the young man chambers a round. name: Zus Learns of Sonia's Death After Horodyszcze Massacre
description: Two young men, Peretz and Jacov, emerge from the forest, their clothes torn and dirty, one holding a rifle. They ask for food, and after a tense exchange, reveal they are survivors from Horodyszcze. Jacov says that two days ago, three thousand Jews lived there—now only fifty remain. He and Peretz had hidden in a wall to survive. Zus asks if they knew his wife, Sonia Bielski. The men exchange a look. Jacov says they knew her. Zus hesitates, then asks about a child. Jacov shakes his head and says, 'Sorry.' Zus leans against a tree and begins to beat his head against it, blood streaming down his face. Asael tells the newcomers, 'His family.' Tuvia moves to Zus and wraps his arms around him. The two brothers weep together, their faces wet with tears. Zus asks why their parents were killed while they survived, saying he should have been there to protect them. Tuvia holds him, saying only, 'No.' After a time, Zus pulls away from Tuvia and walks off into the camp.

Zus walks by with a dark-haired woman named Rona, introducing her as his forest wife. Tuvia offers congratulations, and Malbin comments on the persistence of certain things despite the war.
